pattern.crimePattern: a former partner who skimmed a women's beadwork group's lodge payments kills its chairwoman after she moves the money into the group's own account
pattern.notes: Fictional group, lodge and people. The homestead routine is the evidence: the case never shows the death. The herd boy who found her is a witness only, and is not questioned on screen.

ob.text: Herd boys report a woman found dead in a dry riverbed (lugga) near Archer's Post at 07:30: Nashipai Lenanyokie (33), chairwoman of the Nkaron Women's Beadwork Group.

people.name: Nashipai Lenanyokie
people.bio: Her group's collars sell in every lodge on the river. Fetches water every afternoon, milks at dusk, lights her fire at dark.

facts.text: Nashipai Lenanyokie was found dead in the lugga near Archer's Post at 07:30 on Sunday.
She lay on the sand of the lugga with one blow to the head.
Her two water jerrycans lay beside her: one filled, one empty.
Her phone and KSh 1,800 were still on her.
The lugga is flat, soft sand: no rocks, no bank to fall against.
Ewoi: one pickup with a worn front-left tyre turned at the crossing and left; the edges are softened by the night wind, so it came before the wind rose at about 20:00.
Ewoi: soft sand keeps every foot. Hers walked in; nobody else walked to the lugga.
Her hearth is cold. The firewood bundle she tied that morning is untied and untouched.
Her milk gourds are empty and clean; the kids were left with their mothers all night.
Nolari: Nashipai milked at half past six when the goats came home and lit her fire at dusk. Every day.
Nolari: she fetched water from the lugga every afternoon, two jerrycans, and carried both home full.
Nolari: the household ate the evening meal at about seven.
Nolari: she watched Nashipai leave for the lugga with her jerrycans at about 17:15.
Nolari was at her own homestead all afternoon, and milked her goats at 18:30 in full view of the women. At 19:00 she heard Nashipai's goats crying and thought she was at a meeting.
Nolari: in April the group won a lodge order that had been Mueni Ndolo's.
Nolari: Nashipai complained to the lodge's head office that its purchasing manager, Victor Kiprotich, demanded kickbacks.
Nolari: there is no land quarrel between the homesteads. "We share one fence and one well."
The lodge contract was amended on Friday: payments now go to the group's own account, signed by Nashipai and Nolari.
Lekishon to Nashipai, Friday 21:14: "You will regret what you did to me in front of everybody."
Lekishon's pickup: the front-left tyre is worn bald on the inner edge, with river sand in the treads.
In the cab, behind the seat: Lekishon's rungu, washed, with something dark in a crack in the knob.
Staff-bar till roll: Lekishon's first drink was rung up at 19:34 on Saturday.
Records, Lekishon's line: the mast covers the town and the river; at 20:10 he sent KSh 2,000 to Moses Lekuuk.
Mueni's customers and her church group: in her shop until 19:00, then at a church meeting.
Lodge roster: Victor on duty 14:00–22:00, signing guest requests every hour; suspended pending inquiry from Friday.
Bar roster: Moses behind the bar from 16:00 on Saturday.
Post-mortem: one blow from a heavy, rounded wooden object.
Post-mortem: death on Saturday, broadly between 16:00 and 21:00.
Post-mortem: an empty stomach. She had not eaten the evening meal.
Post-mortem: no animal injuries, no strangulation.
Lab: Nashipai's blood in the crack of Lekishon's rungu.
Missing: her fire was never lit and her goats were never milked.
Missing: her stomach was empty. She never ate the evening meal.
Missing: one jerrycan was never filled.
Missing: nobody walked to the lugga but her.
Missing: nothing was taken from her.
Lekishon: "I went to her homestead at half past six to talk. She was cooking. Then I drove to the lodge bar."
Lekishon: he went to the lugga. "I wanted her to say it to my face, without the women. She said it. I have nothing more."
Lekishon: "I never raised my rungu to her."

Moses: Lekishon came at half past seven, sent him two thousand and said, "If they ask, it was six."

Victor: "I was on duty."
Victor: "She complained about me to head office. She was right. I was suspended on Friday. I didn't leave the lodge."

reconstruction.text: For six years Lekishon drives the group's beadwork to the lodges and keeps "a manager's share" nobody agreed to. In May Nashipai ends their relationship; on Friday she moves the lodge contract into the group's own account. At 21:14 he texts her a threat.
Saturday, about 17:15. Nashipai leaves for the lugga with two jerrycans, as she does every afternoon.
Lekishon drives to the crossing. They argue; she says the women are done with him. He strikes her with his rungu and drives away.
At 18:30 her goats come home and cry to be milked. Her fire is never lit.
19:34. He walks into the lodge staff bar. At 20:10 he sends the barman KSh 2,000: "If they ask, it was six."

clockPlan.note: One stamp: records on Lekishon. Detain him after his story breaks; the rungu trace takes 12 h plus 4 h transport. The post-mortem is at Isiolo, an hour and a half away, and runs in parallel.

ui.beatNotes: Routines as evidence. Nolari's statement becomes a day-strip of Nashipai's routine (water, goats, fire, meal). The player drags absence cards onto it; the strip greys out everything after 17:15, and the time-of-death window on the board narrows from 16:00–21:00 to 17:15–18:30 with a soft click.
